This #NationalNursesWeek, we’re grateful for their compassion, competence, and strength. https://t.co/I1oC4nSJ9K

We can protect Medicaid for those who truly need it by remembering that the 26-year-old, healthy, childless man who’s watching TV at home (and making you pay for his health care) has the responsibility to work.

Those able-bodied people can keep their Medicaid benefits, but they should have to work 20 hours a week to contribute to their communities.

Ohioans are going to work every day— in factories, in construction, as nurses. And they’re paying for their neighbors’ Medicaid.

Able-bodied, childless adults can and should work to help pay for those benefits.

That’s part of making America healthier and driving down costs so that we can protect citizens who are truly vulnerable.

The federal government spends almost $2 trillion on health care every year.

We have to maintain quality AND reduce the cost of delivering health care for our citizens.

After all, time is money. And competition benefits patients. https://t.co/0G7ZsmqOhk

Thank you to the thousands of Ohioans who joined my telephone town hall last night! 

We covered a range of issues affecting hardworking Ohioans, including VA coverage, Medicaid, immigration, and making life more affordable for families.

Customer service is my commitment to Ohio, and it was an honor to hear from so many of you in real time.
Wonderful to meet with patients and families from @OhioChildHosp and hear stories from young Ohioans who’ve beat impossible odds with care from children’s hospitals. https://t.co/PJo30UNRIx

Marilyn joined my telephone town hall with concerns about Medicaid, and I was thankful for the chance to reassure her that Republicans are working to save the program.

One of the common-sense ways we can protect Marilyn’s benefits is to make sure that no one who is in the U.S. illegally can keep draining the program at the expense of American citizens.

Another story of how Obamacare is making life harder for kids with special needs. Republicans are trying to save Medicaid for families like this one.

https://t.co/d4ypyxJrYa https://t.co/JNYf3Rmdkp

Met with @McKesson CEO Brian Tyler to discuss their work in Ohio, including the @CoverMyMeds headquarters in Columbus and the thousands of Ohioans they employ and patients they serve across the state. https://t.co/PArppKgTcH

What are the things that we can do to save Medicaid?

To start, let's stop paying for illegal immigrants to get those benefits at the expense of U.S. citizens.

That will also save American taxpayers money. https://t.co/h27MRcZBqH

Democrats want Ohio taxpayers to bankroll American health care for illegal criminals. 

Senate Republicans want to protect Medicaid for hardworking citizens and those who truly need it.

The federal government has wasted $1.1 TRILLION on fraudulent Medicaid payments. 

Senate Republicans want to root out waste, fraud, and abuse to protect Medicaid for the vulnerable Americans who need it.

If someone isn’t eligible for Medicaid, they shouldn’t be getting generous benefits at the expense of sick, disabled, pregnant Americans and hardworking taxpayers. 

But the abuse of Medicaid is widespread, and Republicans are working to end that abuse. https://t.co/j8q08HdZmN

The truth about Medicaid: “Republicans are doing the country a fiscal and cultural favor by shoring up the program for the poor and disabled.”

https://t.co/f5KGX6ysJ8
